title: Your Bank Can Now Help Companies Buy Other Businesses: RBI's New Rule
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has changed rules for how banks can lend money. Indian banks can now directly fund companies that want to buy other businesses.

faq.a: It means buying enough shares or assets to gain significant influence or decision-making power over another company, often leading to majority ownership.

faq.q: Are there any restrictions on which companies can be acquired with these loans?
faq.a: Yes, the company being acquired must be a "non-financial target." This means it should not be another bank, a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), or any other entity primarily involved in financial services.

faq.q: What happens if the acquiring company fails to repay the loan?
faq.a: Like any other corporate loan, if the borrower company defaults, the bank will follow its standard recovery procedures. This might involve taking over the assets or shares that were pledged as security for the loan.

faq.q: Does this mean banks will now actively encourage companies to merge and acquire?
faq.a: Banks will likely offer this as a new financing product to their corporate clients, supporting their growth strategies. While it facilitates M&A, the decision to merge or acquire ultimately rests with the companies themselves.
